reference_id: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures
reference_title: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures, 1993 Edition
note: This document has NO front-matter 'List of Figures' section (confirmed: the Table of Contents goes directly from Executive Summary to Part I). Unlike other references in this repo, this catalog was NOT built from a List of Figures -- it was hand-built during content-driven reading of Part I Ch.4 (Reliability), Part II Ch.2-3 (Design Requirements / Structural Design, the core design nomographs), and one figure each from Appendices D and G. Every entry's pdf_page_index was directly verified by rendering that page (page_estimated is false for all entries). Coverage is a deliberate subset, not the full ~150+ figures in the guide (Parts III/IV and most appendices are not catalogued).

figures.caption: Serviceability Index (p) Versus Equivalent Load Applications (N)
figures.description: Defines the basic points (p1, pt, Nt) on the pavement serviceability history curve used throughout the Part I reliability derivation.

figures.caption: Basic Points and Deviations for Design-Performance Reliability
figures.description: Shows the four basic ESAL/log-ESAL points (Nt, wT, Wt, Nt) and the Level-0/Level-1 basic deviations (traffic prediction error, reliability design factor log FR, performance prediction error) that compose the reliability framework.

figures.caption: Basic Probability Distributions for Design-Performance Reliability
figures.description: Normal probability distributions for the traffic-prediction and performance-prediction chance deviations, and their sum (overall deviation delta_o).

figures.caption: Definition of Reliability and Evaluation of Reliability Design Factor
figures.description: Derives ZR = (-log FR)/So and FR = 10^(-ZR*So) from the overall deviation distribution; reliability level R = 100*Prob[delta_o >= 0]. Basis for Table 4.1 (standard_normal_deviate_zr).

figures.caption: Illustration of Approach to Identifying the Optimum Reliability Level for a Given Facility
figures.description: Qualitative cost-vs-reliability curves (initial cost increasing, future/distress cost decreasing, total cost minimized) illustrating why an 'optimum' reliability level exists for a given project's usage/risk.

figures.caption: Example Plot of Cumulative 18-kip ESAL Traffic Versus Time
figures.description: Worked example converting a cumulative-traffic-vs-time curve into the design ESAL value used for stage construction / rehabilitation timing analysis.

figures.caption: A Conceptual Example of the Environmental Serviceability Loss Versus Time Graph that may be Developed for a Specific Location
figures.description: Shows cumulative serviceability loss from swelling and frost heave (summed to total environmental loss) versus time; used in the Table 3.1 stage-construction iterative procedure for roadbed swelling/frost heave.

figures.caption: Chart for Estimating Effective Roadbed Soil Resilient Modulus for Flexible Pavements Designed Using the Serviceability Criteria
figures.description: Nomograph pairing monthly roadbed Mr with relative damage uf via uf=1.18e8*MR^-2.32 (digitized exactly in equations.relative_damage_uf); averaging uf over 12 months and inverting gives the effective design MR.

figures.caption: Chart for Estimating Effective Roadbed Soil Resilient Modulus for Flexible Pavements Designed Using the Serviceability Criteria (worked example)
figures.description: Fully worked 12-month example: monthly MR values (20000,20000,2500,4000,4000,7000,7000,7000,7000,7000,4000,20000 psi), sum(uf)=3.72, avg uf=0.31 -> effective MR=5,000 psi. Validation anchor for equations.effective_roadbed_resilient_modulus.

figures.caption: Chart for Estimating Structural Layer Coefficient of Dense-Graded Asphalt Concrete Based on the Elastic (Resilient) Modulus
figures.description: a1 vs EAC (psi) curve, 100,000-500,000 psi (dashed extrapolation above ~420,000 psi, with the guide cautioning against modulus values above 450,000 psi). Digitized as 9 interpolation anchor points in tables.layer_coefficient_a1_asphalt.

figures.caption: Variation in Granular Base Layer Coefficient (a2) with Various Base Strength Parameters
figures.description: 5-scale alignment nomograph (a2, CBR, R-value, Texas Triaxial class, elastic modulus). Superseded in this module by the printed closed-form regression on the following page: a2=0.249*log10(EBS)-0.977 (equations.layer_coefficient_a2_granular_base), verified against the chart's own worked check (EBS=30,000 psi -> a2=0.14).

figures.caption: Variation in Granular Subbase Layer Coefficient (a3) with Various Subbase Strength Parameters
figures.description: Same 5-scale alignment-nomograph style as Figure 2.6, for subbase. Superseded by the printed closed-form regression a3=0.227*log10(ESB)-0.839 (equations.layer_coefficient_a3_granular_subbase), verified against the chart's own worked check (ESB=15,000 psi -> a3=0.11).

figures.caption: Variation in a2 for Cement-Treated Bases with Base Strength Parameter
figures.description: Alignment nomograph, a2 vs 7-day unconfined compressive strength (and an alternate elastic modulus scale). No printed closed-form equation; digitized at 3 dashed cross-alignment points in tables.layer_coefficient_a2_cement_treated.

figures.caption: Variation in a2 for Bituminous-Treated Bases with Base Strength Parameter
figures.description: Alignment nomograph, a2 vs Marshall stability (and an alternate elastic modulus scale). Digitized at 3 dashed cross-alignment points in tables.layer_coefficient_a2_bituminous_treated.

figures.caption: Design Chart for Flexible Pavements Based on Using Mean Values for Each Input
figures.description: THE core flexible design nomograph, printed with its solved equation log10(W18)=ZR*So+9.36*log10(SN+1)-0.20+[log10(dPSI/2.7)]/[0.40+1094/(SN+1)^5.19]+2.32*log10(MR)-8.07, plus a worked example (W18=5e6, R=95%, So=0.35, MR=5000psi, dPSI=1.9 -> SN=5.0). Digitized exactly in equations.flexible_w18_from_sn / flexible_sn_from_w18.

figures.caption: Procedure for Determining Thicknesses of Layers Using a Layered Analysis Approach
figures.description: D*1>=SN1/a1, D*2>=(SN2-SN1*)/(a2*m2), D*3>=(SN3-(SN1*+SN2*))/(a3*m3) minimum-thickness cascade. Digitized in equations.minimum_layer_thicknesses.

figures.caption: Chart for Estimating Composite Modulus of Subgrade Reaction, k(infinity), Assuming a Semi-Infinite Subgrade Depth
figures.description: 4-quadrant turning-line nomograph (roadbed MR + subbase modulus/thickness -> composite k, semi-infinite subgrade). Digitized in composite_k.composite_k_subbase (chart-read anchor grid); the full seasonal worksheet is composite_k.effective_modulus_subgrade_reaction; the no-subbase simplification remains equations.modulus_subgrade_reaction_simple.

figures.caption: Chart to Modify Modulus of Subgrade Reaction to Consider Effects of Rigid Foundation Near Surface (Within 10 ft)
figures.description: Rigid-foundation (bedrock within 10 ft) correction to the composite k: roadbed MR + subgrade depth to rigid foundation DSG -> modified k. Digitized in composite_k.k_rigid_foundation_correction (chart-read).

figures.caption: Chart for Estimating Relative Damage to Rigid Pavements Based on Slab Thickness and Underlying Support
figures.description: Seasonal relative damage u_r vs projected slab thickness D and composite k (log-log fan of D curves). Implemented in composite_k.relative_damage_rigid (closed form reconstructed from later literature -- not printed in this scan -- validated against the guide's printed Table 3.3 worked example and direct chart reads).

figures.caption: Correction of Effective Modulus of Subgrade Reaction for Potential Loss of Subbase Support
figures.description: Loss-of-support correction: effective k (from Table 3.2 worksheet) + LS factor (0-3, Table 2.7 by material) -> corrected design k. Digitized in composite_k.k_loss_of_support (chart-read curves); LS values in composite_k.loss_of_support_values.

figures.caption: Design Chart for Rigid Pavement Based on Using Mean Values for Each Input Variable (Segment 1)
figures.description: First segment of THE core rigid design nomograph, printed with its solved equation and a worked example (k=72pci, Ec=5e6psi, Sc'=650psi, J=3.2, Cd=1.0, So=0.29, R=95%, dPSI=1.7, W18=5.1e6 -> D=10.0in). Digitized exactly in equations.rigid_w18_from_d / rigid_d_from_w18.

figures.caption: Continued--Design Chart for Rigid Pavements Based on Using Mean Values for Each Input Variable (Segment 2)
figures.description: Second segment of the rigid design nomograph (design slab thickness D vs W18 traffic, reliability/So); completes the Figure 3.7 worked example (D=10.0 in).

figures.caption: Computation of the Truck Load Factor for 5 Axle or Greater Trucks on Flexible Pavements with an SN = 5 and a Terminal Serviceability of 2.5
figures.description: Worked example converting a W-4 axle-weight distribution into a single truck load factor using Table D.4 load equivalency factors, illustrating the Appendix D ESAL-conversion workflow (see tables.esal_flexible_single_axle/tandem_axle for the digitized SN=5, pt=2.5 factors).

figures.caption: Nomograph for Estimating Swell Rate Constant
figures.description: Swell rate constant theta from moisture supply and soil fabric fractions (straight-line alignment chart). Digitized in environmental.swell_rate_constant_theta.

figures.caption: Chart for Estimating Potential Vertical Rise of Natural Soils
figures.description: Potential vertical rise VR from plasticity index, moisture condition, and layer thickness (two-panel chart). Coarse chart read in environmental.potential_vertical_rise (calibrated to the printed anchor; ~20-40% stated tolerance).

figures.caption: Chart for Estimating Serviceability Loss Due to Roadbed Swelling
figures.description: Nomograph solving the PRINTED equation dPSI_sw = 0.00335*VR*Ps*(1-e^(-theta*t)) (Ps in percent). Digitized exactly in environmental.swelling_serviceability_loss (printed worked example t=15, theta=0.10, Ps=60%, VR=2in -> 0.3 reproduced).

figures.caption: Chart for Estimating Frost Heave Rate for Subgrade Soil
figures.description: Frost heave rate phi (mm/day) by USCS group and percent finer than 0.02 mm, with the frost-susceptibility classification bar. Coarse chart read in environmental.frost_heave_rate_group / frost_susceptibility_classification.

figures.caption: Graph for Estimating Maximum Serviceability Loss Due to Frost Heave
figures.description: dPSI_MAX vs depth of frost penetration, five drainage-quality lines (linear through the origin, slopes 0.10-0.50 per ft). Digitized exactly in environmental.max_serviceability_loss_frost (printed anchor: poor drainage, 5 ft -> 2.0).

figures.caption: Chart for Estimating Serviceability Loss Due to Frost Heave
figures.description: Nomograph solving the PRINTED equation dPSI_FH = 0.01*PF*dPSI_MAX*(1-e^(-0.02*phi*t)) (PF in percent; the 0.02 constant renders as '02' in the scan and is confirmed by the printed worked example t=15, phi=5, PF=30%, dPSI_MAX=2.0 -> 0.47). Digitized exactly in environmental.frost_heave_serviceability_loss.
